function: Predicts RIS phase shifts, BS transmit and receive beamformers, and UL and DL transmit powers to maximize the weighted sum rate of a full-duplex system (p. 1, 4).
system: Full-duplex BS, ULA with 10 transmit and 10 receive antennas; two passive reflecting RISs of 36 elements; single-antenna users; 3.5 GHz (p. 3, 9, 10).
method: Reinforcement learning: DDPG actor-critic with feature extractor and sub-networks, trained online; first-stage least-squares self-interference cancellation; quantized and grouped RIS phase variants (p. 4, 5, 8).
data_channel: Custom simulator, no dataset: Rician BS-RIS and RIS-user links (K = 9, 6 dB), Rayleigh for others, Jakes time-varying NLOS, path loss from a 5G report (p. 9).
test_conditions: Online training and testing in the same simulated environment; static and moving users; antenna counts 6, 10, 14 change the network input size (p. 6, 9, 11).
baselines: Non-learned: random RIS phases and beamformers (RandPSBF). Learned: DDPG with ZF beamformers using perfect or noisy CSI, DDPG with OU noise, DRL method [32] (p. 9, 10, 12).
metrics: UL and DL data rates in bits/s/Hz over training episodes and as CDFs; signaling bits from BS to RIS; FLOPs (p. 9, 11, 13).
complexity: FLOPs formulas for actor and critic; Table II gives 2.9e4 (PerfCSI-DRL), 3.3e4 (MSF-DRL), 5.46e4 (quantized variants) FLOPs (p. 13).
q1_support: p. 9: "as Rician with the Rician K-factors" - custom simulator with Rician and Rayleigh fading and Jakes Doppler; only the path loss comes from [56], a 5G channel model report; no 3GPP TR 38.901, other standard model, or measured data.
q2_support: p. 11: "Note that the trained DRL" agents are evaluated on rates from the same simulated setup; Fig. 6 varies antennas, but the network input size depends on Mt and Mr (p. 6), so nothing trained is tested in a new condition.
q3_support: p. 12: "method with [32] in Fig. 8" - earlier learned DRL method [32] compared on UL and DL rate; p. 9: "It tries to randomly predict" (RandPSBF, random RIS phases and beamformers) is the non-learned baseline.
q4_support: p. 13: "of floating point operations (FLOPs) at the feature extractor" - FLOP formulas for all networks, and Table II lists 2.9e4, 3.3e4 and 5.46e4 FLOPs.
q5_support: p. 9: "the channels are evolved by Markov Chain Monte Carlo" - channels are generated by the authors' own simulator; the full text gives no code or data link and uses no public channel dataset.
notes: Included, area 3: DDPG learns RIS phases, BS beamformers and powers in a full-duplex system with two RISs (p. 3-4). Path loss follows [56], a 5G channel model report, which is not 3GPP TR 38.901 (p. 9). Learned baseline [32] is compared in Fig. 8 on UL and DL rate (p. 12).
